about:
Montana Steel Industries operates from Belgrade, Montana, tracing its roots to 1944 when Midwest Welding and Machine, Inc. began in a blacksmith shop near downtown Bozeman. The structural steel division was purchased in 2006 to form Midwest Steel Industries, which was renamed Montana Steel Industries in 2014 to avoid confusion with other firms.

The company provides structural, architectural, industrial, and custom steel fabrication. It holds AISC certification for Building Standard, Bridge, and Bridge Component categories, employs a Certified Welding Inspector, and follows an AISC-approved quality manual. Its facility on Dry Creek Road handles projects ranging from ornamental handrails and stairs to large-scale industrial components for hydro-power, dam construction, mining, and renewable energy.

Customers include general contractors, architects, owners, and other fabricators across the western United States. The firm has supplied steel for commercial, residential, and industrial projects such as the Osborne Building in Bozeman, as well as hydro-power facilities, fish passage systems, wind and solar installations, and oil and gas infrastructure.

Montana Steel Industries emphasizes knowledge, accuracy, personable service, and punctual deliveries, earning a reputation as a “Fabricator of Choice” among top regional contractors. The company cites its high repeat-business rate and willingness to tackle challenging custom projects as key differentiators.
